messages:
Miguel: Quick heads up — my flight got delayed and I also just got paged for the latency spike on the inference-router. I need someone to take primary tonight 18:00-02:00 PST. Incident is still warm but not customer-facing yet. runbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/infra/latency-spike

oncall-bot: Incident "INF-7723 latency-surge" paged Miguel at 2026-03-15T16:12:03Z — 12% error rate on model-rtr-1, increased tail latency. Pager severity: P2. Related alerts: cpu-sched-starve, kv-cache-miss-rate.

Priya: I can take _primary_ for the window. Can you drop the quick context and the checklist? :+1:

Miguel: thanks @Priya — tl;dr: some recent deploy touched batching config on model-rtr-1. Symptoms: tail > 500ms, 5xx from kernel timeout. No customer 4xx yet. Action items for primary handoff:
- verify canary rollback status
- monitor tail latency and error budget in dashboard
- if errors > 10% or >5m sustained, escalate to infra-rt
- keep secondary in the loop for hotfixes (we usually call Jordan)

Miguel: Quick commands:
```bash
# check active canary jobs
kubectl -n inference get jobs -l canary=true
# tail logs for model routing pod
kubectl -n inference logs -f deploy/model-rtr-1
# circuit breaker status
curl -s http://ops-metrics.internal/circuit/model-rtr-1/status | jq
```

Sasha: Who's going to be secondary? Jordan is around for the evening but ping him before finalizing. Also remind primary to keep the 15m incident notes updated in the channel.

Miguel: tagging Jordan now — @Jordan will you be secondary 18:00-02:00 PST? If busy we can split.

Jordan: I can be secondary. Will watch the reroute and be ready to cut the emergency rollback if needed. Can you drop the specific rollback command?

Miguel: rollback (if canary shows errors):
```bash
# rollback to stable tag
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/model-rtr-1 model-rtr=redwood/model-rtr:stable-20260228
# then scale down canary pods
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-rtr-canary --replicas=0
```

Priya: Got it. Quick Q: is KV cache enabled for this model variant? If not we should enable prefix-caching to reduce token compute on hot paths.

Miguel: cache was off for that deploy (that was the cause). I've already pushed a hotpatch flag but not a full rollout — primary should validate that enabling prefix cache doesn't blow memory on the p4s. Notes in runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/infra/latency-spike#kv-cache

deploy-bot: Canary rollback job started by Miguel at 2026-03-15T16:25:41Z — job id canary-rollback-7723. See https://ci.redwood/jobs/canary-rollback-7723

Priya: I'll pick up primary at 18:00. Miguel — can you put the handoff summary in the incident doc (15m note) before you go? I'll also post the checklist when I take over.

Miguel: will do in 10m. Leaving the active incident link: https://incidents.redwood/INF-7723

Sasha: small reminder for the on-call checklist: whoever is primary, please: set your Slack status to "ONCALL - primary"; update the pager escalation ETA; and ping support if we need to preemptively open an enterprise ticket.

Priya: setting status now. Also adding a watch rule in the console for tail-latency > 400ms to page Jordan if sustained 3m.

Jordan: ack. I'll standby for rollback coordination and will monitor the anomaly dashboards.

Miguel: thanks team — leaving in 12m. Priya, Jordan — ping me if you want me to run the first rollback step before I leave. Otherwise I'm handing off. :airplane:

Priya: I can run the first validation and then we will coordinate rollback if needed. Thanks Miguel. :thumbsup:

Miguel: Handoff complete — primary swapped to Priya for 18:00-02:00 PST. Secondary Jordan. Leaving short notes in incident doc and the runbook.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: primary=Priya (18:00-02:00 PST), secondary=Jordan. Handoff message archived to incident INF-7723.

Priya: confirmed — primary ownership now. I'll update the post-incident follow-up items tomorrow (batching config rollback, add KV cache test in e2e, tighten canary thresholds).

Sasha: nice clean handoff, thanks everyone. :rocket:
